decisions.title: One obvious primary action per view
decisions.decision: Every view declares one primary action. Secondary actions stay visually and cognitively quieter. If everything is primary, nothing is.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-1 — One obvious primary action. Interaction hierarchy law not previously citeable as GOV.

evidence.quote: Every view declares one primary action. Secondary actions stay visually and cognitively quieter. If everything is primary, nothing is.

decisions.implementation_impact: Each screen/sheet names one primary CTA. Demote competing accents. Motion hierarchy (GOV-112) may support but not invent a second primary.

decisions.title: Reduce decisions — defer choice; infer with correction before asking
decisions.decision: If a choice can wait, it waits. If AI can infer with a correction path, do not ask upfront. Kill List fields stay dead.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-3 — Reduce decisions. Elevates deferral/inference order beyond GOV-032 disclosure and GOV-074 Kill List.

evidence.quote: If a choice can wait, it waits. If AI can infer with correction, do not ask upfront. Kill List fields stay dead.

decisions.implementation_impact: Default to fewer asks. Prefer infer+correct over upfront pickers. Consult Kill List before new fields. Watch chip fatigue (Known risks).

decisions.title: Context before controls — orient before toolbars
decisions.decision: Orient the user (what is this moment for?) before presenting a toolbar of possibilities. Capture bar before settings. Briefing before widget garage.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-5 — Context before controls. Reading/capture orientation law.

evidence.quote: Orient the user (what is this moment for?) before presenting a toolbar of possibilities. Capture bar before settings. Briefing before widget garage.

decisions.implementation_impact: Lead with moment purpose + capture path. Do not open on settings/widget garages. Density modes (GOV-109) must still orient first.

decisions.title: Optimistic where safe; branded confirm where destructive
decisions.decision: Habit toggles and other low-stakes recoverable writes may be optimistic. Account delete, vault wipe, irreversible money, and privacy-affecting shares confirm — branded dialog, typed confirm when stakes peak.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-12 — Optimistic where safe; confirm where destructive. Elevates optimistic path beside existing confirm canon (GOV-015/065).

sections: IX-12 — Optimistic where safe; confirm where destructive
evidence.quote: Habit toggles may be optimistic. Account delete, vault wipe, irreversible money, and privacy-affecting shares confirm — branded dialog, typed confirm when stakes peak.

decisions.implementation_impact: Classify writes: optimistic vs confirm-required. Keep branded ConfirmDialog; ban window.confirm. Pair optimistic UI with honest sync states.

decisions.title: Infer then chip — correction chips are first-class UI
decisions.decision: Pre-filled structure shows chips for correction. Chips are first-class UI, not afterthoughts.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-13 — Infer, then chip. Operationalizes correctable inference as visible chip affordances.

evidence.quote: Pre-filled structure shows chips for correction. Chips are first-class UI, not afterthoughts.

decisions.implementation_impact: Ship chip patterns for inferred fields. Do not hide correction in buried edit menus. Mitigate chip fatigue (REC + Known risks).

decisions.title: Capture beats navigation — Palette/Logger outrank deep-link tourism
decisions.decision: Getting data in beats touring the information architecture. Command Palette / Logger outrank deep-link tourism for daily intents.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-14 — Capture beats navigation. Elevates daily capture primacy beyond GOV-028/059.

evidence.quote: Getting data in beats touring the information architecture. Palette/Logger outrank deep-link tourism for daily intents.

decisions.implementation_impact: Prioritize capture entry points over nav tourism. Depends on GOV-099 palette scope still Needs Discussion — founder align via REC.

decisions.title: Undo over fear — recoverable mistakes get undo; unrecoverable get confirm
decisions.decision: Prefer undo windows for recoverable mistakes; prefer confirm for unrecoverable ones. Do not use fear copy for recoverable acts.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-16 — Undo over fear. Error-recovery / editing law missing from prior GOVs.

evidence.quote: Prefer undo windows for recoverable mistakes; prefer confirm for unrecoverable ones. Do not use fear copy for recoverable acts.

decisions.implementation_impact: Add undo windows for recoverable deletes/edits where feasible. Keep confirm for irreversible. Tone: calm agency, not fear.

decisions.title: Shortcuts are progressive enhancement — never the only essential path
decisions.decision: Keyboard chords (e.g. ⌘K, Space→L, Esc) accelerate; they never become the only path for essential capture on desktop. Mobile provides equivalent one-thumb primary paths.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-17 — Shortcuts are progressive enhancement. Keyboard + cross-platform path law.

evidence.quote: Chords (`⌘K`, `Space→L`, `Esc`) accelerate; they never become the only path for essential capture on desktop. Mobile has equivalent one-thumb primary paths.

decisions.implementation_impact: Every essential capture has visible primary control. Shortcuts documented/taught (Known risks). Mobile: one-thumb primary, not chord-dependent.

decisions.title: Forms are a last resort — NL + chips + progressive fields default
decisions.decision: Natural language + chips + progressive fields beat multi-field forms as the default personality. Forms remain for high-stakes accuracy when needed — not as default.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-18 — Forms are a last resort. Elevates positive default beyond GOV-008 refuse form-builder.

sections: IX-18 — Forms are a last resort
evidence.quote: NL + chips + progressive fields beat six-field finance as the only path. Forms remain for high-stakes accuracy when needed — not as default personality.

decisions.implementation_impact: Default capture = NL/chips/progressive. Multi-field forms only when stakes demand accuracy. Do not revive form-builder personality.

decisions.title: Consistency of verbs — same action, same verb across surfaces
decisions.decision: The same action uses the same verb across surfaces (e.g. Save, Log, Complete, Delete). Verb drift is interaction debt.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-20 — Consistency of verbs. Interaction naming law pending Naming Language artifact.

evidence.quote: Same action uses same verb across surfaces (Save, Log, Complete, Delete). See Naming Language.

decisions.implementation_impact: Align button/menu verbs across web/native. Govern full lexicon in Naming Language (next). No synonym salad for same act.

decisions.title: Latency honesty — skeleton for waits; never fake instant if pending
decisions.decision: Use skeleton/progress for known waits. Do not fake instant success if sync is pending — especially on native outbox.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-21 — Latency honesty. Elevates interaction-level honesty beyond GOV-089/121.

evidence.quote: Skeleton/progress for known waits. Do not fake instant if sync is pending — especially on native outbox.

decisions.implementation_impact: Pending/outbox states visible. No success chrome while sync pending. Skeletons for known waits; loading motion not mask (GOV-121).

decisions.title: Accessibility is interaction quality — not a later audit
decisions.decision: Keyboard access, focus order, hit targets, and announcements are part of interaction design — not a later audit.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-22 — Accessibility is interaction quality. Elevates a11y into interaction law (details still in Accessibility Principles).

evidence.quote: Keyboard, focus order, hit targets, and announcements are part of interaction design — not a later audit (see Accessibility Principles).

decisions.implementation_impact: Interaction PRs include focus order, keyboard path, hit targets, announcements. Defer numeric a11y floors to Accessibility Principles + GOV-071/107.

decisions.title: Device-appropriate gestures — platform conventions win
decisions.decision: Platform conventions (back, share sheets, system biometrics) win over reinvented gestures — unless Constitution requires otherwise (e.g. capture ceiling).
decisions.reason: Principle IX-23 — Device-appropriate gestures. Fills gesture gap left open in Motion pass.

evidence.quote: Platform conventions (back, share sheets, system biometrics) win over reinvented gestures — unless Constitution requires otherwise (e.g., capture ceiling).

decisions.implementation_impact: Prefer system back/share/biometrics. Do not invent cousin gestures. /m capture ceiling and native≠/m still bind.

decisions.title: Compression is continuous — estimate interaction delta; net-positive count fails
decisions.decision: New features must estimate interaction delta. A net-positive interaction count for the same outcome is a fail unless stakes demand it.
decisions.reason: Principle IX-25 — Compression is continuous. Elevates continuous delta accounting beyond GOV-034 craft target.

evidence.quote: New features must estimate interaction delta. Net-positive interaction count for the same outcome is a fail unless stakes demand it.
Compression is not a slogan; it is interaction law.

decisions.implementation_impact: Feature proposals include interaction-delta estimate. Ties to GOV-060 Needs Discussion (economy as performance) and eight-gate (GOV-093).

score.interpretation: Interaction Principles operationalize Article V: primary action, decision reduction, context-before-controls, optimistic/confirm, chips, capture-over-nav, undo, shortcuts, forms-last, verbs, latency honesty, a11y-as-interaction, gestures, continuous compression.
